title: Conceptual Singularities
description: Compress an entire field of knowledge into one point. Unlocks the Conceptual Singularity Compressor.

puzzle.goal: A source emits N symbols from an alphabet of k letters, letter j with probability pj. For long messages almost every message has letter j appearing N·pj times; the number of such typical messages is a multinomial coefficient. Write the number of bits per symbol needed to give each typical message its own code word, in the limit of long messages.
puzzle.name: Shannon entropy from typical-sequence counting (source coding)
puzzle.form: lim ( N , ∞ , log ( N ! / prod ( j , 1 , k , ( N * p _ j ) ! ) ) / ( N * log ( 2 ) ) )
puzzle.ask: With Stirling's approximation the limit is H = −Σ pj log₂ pj, and the message needs N·H bits. Find the minimum number of bits for N = @{N} symbols drawn uniformly from k = @{k} letters.
puzzle.method: Count arrangements of a message with fixed letter counts, take log₂ to get the bits needed to index them, apply ln n! ≈ n ln n − n, and divide by N.
